exposure: Fetal growth trajectories (catch-up growth, proportional abdominal circumference-to-femur length growth, disproportional abdominal circumference-to-femur length growth, consistently large)
outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: The participants were 235 large-for-gestational age births from the LIFECODES Fetal Growth Study.
finding: The study identified four multivariate trajectories of fetal growth among large-for-gestational age births, revealing that a 'catch-up growth' subgroup was uniquely associated with pregestational diabetes mellitus and a higher risk of NICU admission, while the 'consistently large' group experienced a lower risk of adverse birth outcomes.
